title: No catch-all for unmatched /api paths — every routing miss answers 1.1KB of Express HTML instead of JSON
evidence: I read server.js end to end. After `app.use('/api', apiRoutes)` (:375), `app.use('/api/v1', apiRoutes)` (:376), `app.use('/api', plotsRouter)` (:377) and `app.use('/api/v1', plotsRouter)` (:378) the next `app.use` is the 4-arg **error** handler at :443, which Express never invokes for an unmatched route. `grep -n "app.use((req\|app.all(\|notFound" server.js` returns only the two sanitizer/request-id middlewares at :132 and :138. routes/api/index.js ends at :457 with `module.exports = router` — no terminal middleware there either. This is the cause of the measured `Cannot GET /api/plots` HTML body.
impact: Every mistyped path, every retired endpoint, and every documented-but-dead path (5 of them — see API-07) returns text/html ~1.1KB instead of JSON. apps/web-app/src/lib/api/api-client.ts:425 gates parsing on `content-type: application/json`, so `data` becomes null, `backendError` becomes '' and the user gets `toUserFriendlyError('', 404)` — a generic string with no path, no code, no requestId. A wrong URL is indistinguishable from a broken server for both the UI and any partner integrator.
verdict_reason: Reproduced every number independently. `git log --oneline -- docs/api/openapi.json` → exactly one commit 23e6a18c dated 2026-05-17 (=114 days before 2026-09-08). `git rev-list --count 23e6a18c..HEAD -- apps/backend/routes` = 334. Regenerated in-memory via require('./config/swagger') and did a leaf-key diff against the file: 126 only-in-published, 14 only-in-regen, 30 differing values — matches exactly. Published = 41 paths / 48 ops; regenerated = 36 paths / 43 ops — matches. Published login op declares required:[healthId,password] with no `identifier` property (confirmed in the JSON); source JSDoc at auth-health.js:38 declares required:[identifier,password] and carries the quoted comment. I ran the real validator: healthLoginSchema.safeParse({healthId:'1101900000005',password:'Abcd1234!'}) → success=false, issue path ['identifier']; the same parse with `identifier` → success=true. middleware/validate.js:23-40 converts that into a 400 VALIDATION_ERROR before the controller. scripts/generate-openapi-spec.js:159-160 does write docs/api/openapi.json.
correction: Two small precisions. (1) Line refs: the login @swagger block is auth-health.js:25-58 with the handler at :59 (cited 30-59); healthLoginSchema is auth-schemas.js:56-82 (cited 56-75). (2) The impact line 'a 400 they cannot diagnose, because the field the spec names does not appear in the error' overstates slightly — validate.js:22-26 emits details[{field:'identifier',...}], so the correct field name IS in the body; what is absent is any mention of `healthId`. The 400 is diagnosable, just not from the spec.

title: HTTP 401 means two different things; the MFA challenge screen is unreachable because of it
evidence: `mapOtpFailure('EXPIRED')` returns `{status:401, body:{success:false, error:'Code expired', code:'OTP_EXPIRED', errorTh:'รหัส OTP หมดอายุ…'}}` (mfa.js:65-75). The web client calls it via `apiClient.post('/api/mfa/verify', …)` with no options (mfa-challenge-form.tsx:80). In api-client.ts:348 `isAuthEndpoint` requires `url.includes('/auth/')`; `baseUrl` defaults to `''` (:141-142) so `url === '/api/mfa/verify'` — no `/auth/`. `suppressAuthRedirect` defaults to `skipAuth` = false (:273). Control therefore reaches :404 `AuthService.clearSession()` and :412 `window.location.href = loginUrl`, returning `{success:false, error:'Session expired. Please sign in again'}` with no `code`. The branch `if (res.code === 'OTP_EXPIRED')` at mfa-challenge-form.tsx:92 can never be true. The sibling branch `res.code === 'OTP_TOO_MANY'` (429, so not intercepted) fails for the separate reason in API-03.
impact: A user who types an OTP one second after it expires is logged out and bounced to the login page, losing the mfa_session token they would need to retry. Both Thai copy strings (`copy.expired`, `copy.tooMany`) are dead. This is the platform's second auth factor on a government service where ThaiD/หมอพร้อม are the target production factors.
verdict_reason: Set-difference between the published file and the regenerated spec returns exactly the five claimed (path,method) pairs and nothing else: /api/farms/{id}/qrcode GET, /api/payments GET, /api/payments/slip/upload POST, /api/payments/slip/{id}/approve POST, /api/pricing/invoice/{phase} GET. Nothing exists only in the regenerated spec. Router verification confirms each: payments.js declares only router.post at :208 /create, :356 /phase1/:applicationId, :463 /phase2/:applicationId, :501 /checkout — zero GET handlers, zero /slip/*. pricing.js declares only router.get :229 '/', :251 '/fees', router.post :291 '/calculate'. farms.js carries the Thai deletion note for the farm-level QR door at :265-269 dated 2026-09-05. POST /api/payments/checkout is absent from the published spec (it is not among the 48 ops) and does carry its own paymentLimiter. Finding is read-only on money paths, as required.

title: The web client throws away the machine-readable error code for 108 of the 121 endpoints that bother to send one
evidence: `const rawCode = String(data?.error || data?.code || '').trim() || undefined;` — `error` wins over `code`. The SAME file at :366 does the opposite for the 401 branch: `String(errorData?.code || errorData?.error || '')`. My envelope scan of all 187 route files found 1072 raw `res.status(>=400).json({…})` sites; 121 carry a top-level `code`, and by key-signature 108 of those also carry `error` (`success,code,error` ×33, `success,error,code` ×25, `success,error,code,message` ×22, `success,code,error,message` ×8, `success,code,permission,error` ×7, `success,code,error,errorTh` ×5, `success,error,code,messageTh` ×4, +4 more). For all 108, `res.code` is set to the human sentence and the real code is dropped (`extractEnvelopeMeta` at :109 strips `code` too, so it is not recoverable from `.meta`). The repo already knows: the comment at api-client.ts:66-72 says "the raw `error:'Forbidden'` would otherwise win the `rawCode = data.error || data.code` harvest below and hide the real code" — and patched it with two hardcoded body-sniffers (`isActiveEntityMismatchBody` :96, `isEntityPermissionDenialBody`) instead of fixing the precedence.
impact: Every `res.code === '…'` branch in the frontend silently never fires for those 108 endpoints. Confirmed dead consumers: mfa-challenge-form.tsx:93 (`OTP_TOO_MANY`, backend mfa.js:76-85 sends both `error` and `code`), close-period-modal.tsx:54/60/70/78, reopen-period-modal.tsx:116-124, QuotationReviewSection.tsx:241, invoice-step.tsx:323, trust-verifier-portal.tsx:48. The user sees the generic fallback copy instead of the specific Thai remediation.
verdict_reason: Workflow confirmed at .github/workflows/generate-api-clients.yml — triggers on push/PR to main+develop for openapi/**/*.yaml (lines 11-22), generates with --skip-validate-spec plus `|| echo "⚠️ Warning"` so nothing can fail it, and lines 112-126 do `git add`/`git commit`/`git push` on push events with [skip ci]. The specs are fictional: authentication-service.yaml servers at :35/:37/:39 are api.gacp.platform, staging-api.gacp.platform, localhost:3001/v1/auth; access-service.yaml :16 and pricing-service.yaml :16 are api.gacp-botanical.com. /api/v2 paths exist in access-service.yaml (:24,:53,:82) and pricing-service.yaml (:24,:49,:76); grep for 'api/v2' across apps/backend/server.js + routes/ returns nothing, and server.js:384 mounts '/api' with the literal comment '(no /v2 prefix)'. payment-service.yaml:295 defines /webhooks/omise; a word-boundary grep for 'omise' across routes/ and services/ returns nothing (the finding's original grep would have matched 'Promise' — I re-ran it with -w and it is genuinely clean). openapi/auth-health.yaml:295-306 defines LoginRequest as required:[email,password], which auth-schemas.js:69-76 explicitly rejects. Output dirs are absent: apps/web-app/src/generated does not exist, apps/mobile_app does not exist (only apps/mobile-app), grep 'generated/api' in apps/web-app/src returns nothing, and @openapitools/openapi-generator-cli is in no package.json. openapitools.json pins 7.17.0 with no generators block and was added in the first commit e94759c1.
correction: 'Eight fictional microservice specs' is one too many for the generation loop. The SERVICES array lists 8 names but one of them, `auth-Applicant`, has no matching openapi/auth-Applicant.yaml, so the `if [ -f ]` guard skips it and only 7 specs are ever generated. openapi/ does hold 8 YAMLs + README, but the 8th is auth-health.yaml, which the workflow never consumes — so the contradictory email-login contract in auth-health.yaml:295-306 is a stale in-repo document, not something this pipeline emits. The deletion recommendation is unaffected.

title: Rate limiters are mounted on hardcoded path strings that no longer match the router tree — /api/v1 bypasses the payment limiter, and the webhook limiter guards a path with no router
evidence: `app.use('/api/payments/checkout', paymentLimiter)` (:333) is a literal prefix match, but apiRoutes is mounted at BOTH `/api` (:375) and `/api/v1` (:376), so `POST /api/v1/payments/checkout` resolves to routes/api/finance/payments.js:501 with only `globalLimiter` in front. The comment directly above at :285-292 says the auth limiters were fixed for exactly this ("EVERY one was trivially bypassed by hitting /api/v1/auth/… (audit M-2)") and the `for (const prefix of ['/api','/api/v1'])` loop at :293 proves the pattern — payments at :325-334 was left out of that loop. Separately, `app.use('/api/callbacks', webhookLimiter)` (:334) and `SANITIZE_BYPASS = /^\/api(?:\/v\d+)?\/callbacks/` (:131) target `/api/callbacks`; `grep -rn callbacks routes/ controllers/ modules/` returns nothing — no router is mounted there. The live webhook is `POST /api/webhooks/stripe` (routes/api/index.js:164 → routes/api/webhooks/stripe.js:60).
impact: paymentLimiter is 10 requests / 5 min (middleware/rate-limiter.js); globalLimiter is 1000 / 15 min (server.js RATE_LIMIT_MAX default). Via the /api/v1 alias an authenticated applicant gets a ~33x larger budget for a route that mints a real Stripe PaymentIntent per call. The Stripe webhook has no per-endpoint limit at all. (Sanitization is not at risk — signature verification reads `req.rawBody`, captured at server.js:121 before the sanitizer.)
verdict_reason: Confirmed on every count. Searching the published spec: zero paths containing 'trace', 'verify', 'public', or 'interoperability' out of 41. The GET /api/certificates description does contain the quoted pointer to '/api/trace/* endpoints — those need no auth' while no such path is in the document. GET /api/harvest-batches/lot/{batchNumber} has parameters and tags but no `responses` key at all. interoperability.js has exactly 14 route declarations and zero @swagger blocks: keyless at :90, :97, :157, :168, :179, :228, :266 (7); requirePartnerApiKey at :104, :197, :285, :343, :452, :477 (6); plus :396 revoke behind authenticatePROVIDER+requireAdminRole. Mounted at routes/api/index.js:350. Partner keys come from middleware/partner-api-key.js:55-62 via x-api-key. public.js:94/:278/:347 and trace.js:62/:86/:125 and trace-batch-lot-routes.js:49/:198 and trace-verification-routes.js:35 all confirmed at the cited lines. certificates.js:486 confirmed. LAB_API_KEY: `grep process.env.LAB_API_KEY` across the backend returns nothing — it appears only in partner-api-key.js:21 (a comment), config/swagger.js:51 and :69. No '/callbacks' router is mounted in routes/api/index.js, yet server.js:343 gives it a webhookLimiter and server.js:131 a sanitizer bypass.

title: 119 distinct response envelope shapes across 187 route files; the shared responder is used by 1.7% of success exits
where: apps/backend/shared/api-response.js (canonical) · apps/backend/shared/response.js (dead) · 1633 raw res.json sites in routes/
evidence: I parsed every `res.json({…})` / `res.status(N).json({…})` object literal in routes/ and collected top-level key signatures: 1633 sites, **62 distinct success signatures** and **57 distinct error signatures**. Success: `{success,data}` ×359, `{success,message,data}` ×52, `{success,count,data}` ×32, `{success,message}` ×15, `{success,data,cached}` ×12, `{success,data,pagination}` ×7, `{success,data,meta}` ×6, `{success,data,count}` ×5, `{data}` alone ×4 (routes/api/documents/sop-documents.js:37), `{success}` alone ×4, down a 62-item tail. Error: `{success,error}` ×626, `{success,message}` ×136, `{success,error,message}` ×103, `{error}` alone ×23 (routes/api/certificates/certificates.js:46). Helper adoption in routes/, excluding require lines: `sendSuccessResponse` 9 call sites vs 515 raw 2xx sites (1.7%); `sendErrorResponse` 19 + `respondError` 150 = 169 vs 1072 raw 4xx/5xx sites (13.6%). A third helper, shared/response.js, defines a FOURTH shape (`{success,message,data}` / `{success,error}`), is re-exported by shared/index.js:6, and has zero consumers anywhere in the repo.
impact: The measured five shapes over 22 endpoints understate it by ~24x. Consumers cannot write one unwrapping path: apps/web-app/src/lib/api/api-client.ts:514 has to do `data?.data ?? data` and then harvest unknown sibling keys into `.meta` (:509-513) because `count`/`total`/`pagination`/`meta`/`summary`/`cached` are four different names for the same idea. Pagination alone is spelled three ways: `count`, `total`, `pagination`.
fix: Do not sweep 1633 sites. Smallest correct root fix, in this order: (1) delete shared/response.js and its shared/index.js:6 export — zero callers, one less shape (trivial); (2) add `scripts/probes/api-envelope.sh` in the repo's existing ratchet style with baseline = today's raw-site count per bucket, one-way down, so no NEW raw envelope can be added; (3) add `sendListResponse(res, req, {items, total, cursor})` to shared/api-response.js so the pagination trio collapses to one name for new code. The 1633-site migration is the follow-up sweep, driven down by the ratchet rather than by a single >10-file PR.
verdict_reason: Recounted over the published file: 48 operations, 18 with no `responses` key at all, and exactly 3 carrying any `content` — GET /api/applications/draft, GET /api/audits, GET /api/auth/health/me. So 45 of 48 have no response schema. Zero operations declare a `default` response. The document contains exactly one $ref (#/components/schemas/User); the other six component schemas (PlantSpecies, HarvestBatch, PreSubmissionValidation, DocumentSlot, PlantUnit, PlantUnitLifecycle) are referenced by nothing. generate-openapi-spec.js:87-101 does collect missing-responses as warnings and writes anyway, carrying the quoted comment. All five measured 404 paths do have routers mounted (index.js:83 master-data, :317 plots, :327 lots, :343 training-records, :355 surveys). The sixth envelope is real: public.js:109-121 returns {success, verified, valid, data:{status, reasonCode, reason}}. The proposed ApiError shape matches shared/api-response.js — respondError/sendErrorResponse emits {success:false, code, error, message, messageTh, details?, requestId, timestamp, path, method} (responseMeta at :80-87, the json() at :124-134).
correction: The second half of the fix is already implemented in this tree and should not be re-proposed as new work. commit fe289fea ('an API that answers HTML has broken its contract'), dated 2026-09-08 02:40 and an ancestor of HEAD, added apps/backend/middleware/api-not-found.js plus server.js:455-457 mounting apiNotFoundHandler on both /api and /api/v1, with an integration test at __tests__/integration/api-answers-json-not-html.test.js. The measured HTML 404 is therefore a stale-deployment fact, not a missing-code fact: the remaining action is to deploy, not to write a handler. title: The committed OpenAPI spec is stale — 5 of its 41 paths no longer exist, including two retired payment-slip endpoints — and nothing in CI regenerates it
evidence: I reassembled the spec in memory from the live JSDoc (`require('apps/backend/config/swagger')`, whose `apis` glob at config/swagger.js:162-166 covers routes/**, controllers/**, server.js) and diffed it against the committed file: live = 36 paths, committed = 41. Present in the committed file, absent from regeneration: `/api/farms/{id}/qrcode`, `/api/payments`, `/api/payments/slip/upload`, `/api/payments/slip/{id}/approve`, `/api/pricing/invoice/{phase}`. I then checked each against the router: routes/api/cultivation/farms.js declares only `/`, `/my`, `/my/eligible-for-planting`, `/:id` — no `/qrcode`; routes/api/finance/payments.js declares only `/create`, `/phase1/:applicationId`, `/phase2/:applicationId`, `/checkout` — no GET `/` and no `/slip/*` (`grep -rn "slip/upload" routes/` returns nothing; the slip rail was retired 2026-09-06); routes/api/finance/pricing.js declares only `/`, `/fees`, `/calculate` — no `/invoice/:phase`. The generator's own header (scripts/generate-openapi-spec.js:21) states "this script is NOT wired into .husky/pre-commit; it's a manual ops command".
impact: 48 documented operations = 7.4% of the 648-handler surface, and 12% of the documented paths are lies that answer Express HTML (API-01) rather than 404 JSON. The live money door — `POST /api/payments/checkout`, the only route that mints a Stripe PaymentIntent — is undocumented, while two retired slip endpoints are published. fix:
Wire drift detection, not a doc-writing sprint. Add to the existing gate (scripts/ci/local-gate.sh, alongside check-orphan-api-routes.js which already runs green):
```sh
node apps/backend/scripts/generate-openapi-spec.js
git diff --exit-code docs/api/openapi.json   # non-zero = spec drifted
```
Run it once now to drop the 5 dead paths, and fix `servers` to the demo/staging hosts. Coverage from 7.4% is a separate, ratcheted campaign — do not block on it.
verdict_reason: Confirmed at the source. The @swagger block above GET /api/audits (routes/api/audit/audits.js:59-95) declares item properties id:{type:integer}, auditNumber, status, plantType, scheduledDate. The handler at :110-121 builds id: app.id and auditNumber: app.applicationNumber from Application rows, and prisma/schema/application.prisma:4 is `id String @id @default(uuid())` — so the wire value is a uuid string. The annotation omits four fields the handler returns: applicationId, applicantName, inspector, auditMode. This is indeed one of only 3 operations in the whole document with a typed response. The parenthetical about the component schemas also holds: PlantSpecies.id and HarvestBatch.id are both declared integer, while trace.prisma:176 and harvest.prisma:9 are both `id String @id @default(uuid())`; HarvestBatch also declares farmId and speciesId as integer.

title: The plots router is mounted twice; one mount produces only phantom URLs and is why GET /api/plots 404s
evidence: routes/api/cultivation/plots.js declares its own full paths — `POST /farms/:farmId/plots` (:37), `GET /farms/:farmId/plots` (:118), `DELETE /plots/:id` (:140) — i.e. it is written to be mounted at the API ROOT, which server.js:377-378 does. routes/api/index.js additionally mounts the same module under `/plots`, yielding `/api/plots/farms/:farmId/plots` and `/api/plots/plots/:id`, and creating no `/api/plots` collection at all. That is exactly the measured `Cannot GET /api/plots`. The real consumer is apps/web-app/src/lib/services/planting-service.ts:80 → `/api/farms/${farmId}/plots`; `grep -rn 'api/plots' apps/web-app/src` returns nothing.
impact: Three phantom URLs on the public surface, a resource whose obvious collection URL (`/api/plots`) is a hole, and a mount-order trap: because plotsRouter is mounted at server.js:377 AFTER apiRoutes, any future catch-all placed inside routes/api/index.js would silently kill the farm's plot list. Doubled again by the /api/v1 alias = 6 phantom URLs.
fix: Delete routes/api/index.js:319 (one line — no consumer). Then either accept that plots live at `/api/farms/:farmId/plots` (correct: a plot belongs to a farm) or, better, move the module's declarations under the farms router so server.js:377-378 can be deleted too and the whole API tree lives in one file. Ship the deletion first; it is what unblocks a safely-placed catch-all for API-01.
verdict_reason: Walked the whole chain. auth-health.js:176 mounts GET /me → AuthController.getMe; the @swagger block above it $refs #/components/schemas/User, which config/swagger.js:137-147 declares with exactly six properties. getMe is controllers/auth-controller/health-auth-profile-handlers.js:308, and lines :319-320 are exactly `const user = await AuthService.getProfile(req.user.id);` / `return sendSuccessResponse(res, req, { data: sanitizeUserPayload(user) });` — the cited line numbers are precise. prisma-auth-service.js:546-548 is `async getProfile(userId) { return await prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { id: userId } }); }` with no `select`. sanitizeUserPayload is auth-controller.js:63-89, a deny-list that spreads the row and deletes exactly ten named fields. I parsed prisma/schema/auth.prisma: model User has 73 scalar columns, and healthId, providerId, canonicalId, canonicalIdLegacy, healthIdHmac, providerIdHmac and taxIdHmac are all present and all absent from the deny-list. 73 − 10 = up to 63 fields on the wire against 6 documented. The finding is explicit that it read the code path only and did not call the endpoint — that honesty is warranted and the claim is scoped to what it proved. The allow-list fix is the right root fix and touches one function plus one schema block.

title: Versioning is decorative — /api/v1 is a byte-identical alias, no negotiation exists, and a breaking change today breaks every client at once
evidence: server.js:375-378 mounts the SAME router object at `/api` and `/api/v1`, so both prefixes are identical for all 648 handlers. middleware/api-version.js sets `req.apiVersion` from the URL (:23) or the `X-API-Version` header (:28) with no validation, and echoes it back verbatim (:37) alongside `X-API-Supported-Versions: 1` (:38) — a client sending `X-API-Version: 9` is told `X-API-Version: 9` and served normally. `requireVersion()` (:47) and `deprecateEndpoint()` (:64) exist and have **zero callers** (`grep -rn 'requireVersion\|deprecateEndpoint' --include=*.js .` outside the defining file returns nothing). Nothing anywhere branches on `req.apiVersion`. Three unrelated version vocabularies coexist: URL `v1`; `GET /api/version` → `{version:'3.0.0', minClientVersion:'1.0.0'}` (routes/api/index.js:447-455); OpenAPI `info.version: 3.0.0`. And two independent `v1` segments nest in one URL — routes/api/integration/interoperability.js:157 declares `/v1/certificates/:n/verify`, so `/api/v1/interoperability/v1/certificates/X/verify` is live.
impact: There is no escape hatch. Any breaking change to a response body or status code lands on every consumer simultaneously — the Next.js app, the public verify page, and any partner integrator holding the published spec. `X-API-Version` gives integrators a false signal that negotiation exists. This is a government certification platform whose partner trace API is already specced (docs/api/partner-trace-api-spec.md).
fix: Either commit to versioning or stop advertising it. Recommended, smallest first: (1) make the header honest — in apiVersionMiddleware, reject `X-API-Version` values not in SUPPORTED_VERSIONS with a 400 `UNSUPPORTED_API_VERSION` rather than echoing them (5 lines in middleware/api-version.js:28-34); (2) rename the interoperability router's internal `/v1/*` segment so only one `v1` can appear in a URL; (3) when a real v2 is needed, mount a SEPARATE router at `/api/v2` and freeze `/api/v1` — the alias structure already supports this, which is the one genuinely good thing about the current setup. title: Prisma's relationJoins is off, so all 167 include-using queries pay one 244 ms round trip per relation
evidence: The generator block declares only prismaSchemaFolder; relationJoins is absent. @prisma/client is ^5.22.0 (package.json), which supports relationJoins as a Preview feature with relationLoadStrategy: 'join' on PostgreSQL. I counted 167 find* calls using `include` across routes/controllers/services/modules. The worst by relation count: services/planting/planting-cycle-detail-loader.js:8 (farm, plantSpecies, certificate, cyclePlots + nested plot, batches + nested _count, cultivationLogs, _count ≈ 9 queries ≈ 2196 ms for one cycle-detail page); services/traceability-service.js:861 (7, see PAY-04); services/invoice-service.js:185 (applicant, application, application.entity, lineItems ≈ 5).
impact: This is the multiplier under PAY-04 and half of PAY-07. Collapsing planting-cycle-detail-loader.js:8 alone from 9 queries to 1 is −1952 ms on the cycle detail page.
fix: Do NOT flip it globally in one step — relationJoins changes the emitted SQL for every include at once and Prisma 5.x has known interactions with `distinct` and some nested filters. Instead: add "relationJoins" to previewFeatures in _base.prisma, regenerate, then opt IN per query on the three hottest reads first — `relationLoadStrategy: 'join'` on planting-cycle-detail-loader.js:8, traceability-service.js:861, invoice-service.js:185 — and re-time each against the current numbers. Roll the rest only after those three are proven. Note this also fixes services/planting/planting-cycle-detail-loader.js:45 where `batches: { include: { _count: ... } }` returns whole HarvestBatch rows while the code reads only id/batchNumber/status/trackingUrl (:117-121) — give it an explicit select at the same time.
verdict_reason: prisma/schema/_base.prisma:4-8 declares previewFeatures = ["prismaSchemaFolder"] only; relationJoins is absent. @prisma/client resolves to 5.22.0 in node_modules (package.json ^5.22.0), which supports relationJoins as Preview with relationLoadStrategy on PostgreSQL. planting-cycle-detail-loader.js:8 is the findUnique and its include carries farm, plantSpecies, certificate, cyclePlots (+nested plot), batches (+nested _count), cultivationLogs and _count — the heaviest include in the read path. The secondary observation is also true: `batches` at :50-56 returns whole HarvestBatch rows while :117-121 reads only id/batchNumber/status/trackingUrl. The staged opt-in advice (per-query relationLoadStrategy first, do not flip globally) is the right shape.
correction: The `_count` selections in that include are aggregate queries and may not fold into a lateral join on 5.22 — so expect the cycle-detail collapse to land nearer 9 → 3 than 9 → 1. Re-time it rather than quoting −1952 ms.

title: Pagination is the exception, not the rule: 20 of 284 collection GET routes accept any pagination parameter; 241 of 325 findMany calls have no row limit

title: Five phantom operations in the published spec — including two retired money endpoints — describe routes that no longer exist in the code
evidence: Set-difference between the published file and the spec regenerated from today's JSDoc: exactly these five (path, method) pairs exist only in the file. Verified each against the router: apps/backend/routes/api/finance/payments.js declares only four routes — `router.post('/create')` :208, `/phase1/:applicationId` :356, `/phase2/:applicationId` :463, `/checkout` :501 — no GET at all and no `/slip/*`. apps/backend/routes/api/finance/pricing.js declares only `/` :229, `/fees` :251, `/calculate` :291 — no `/invoice/:phase`. apps/backend/routes/api/cultivation/farms.js:266-269 carries the deletion note for the QR route (removed 2026-09-05 by operator ruling). The two slip operations match the retired flow recorded in project memory (payment is Stripe-only, settled by webhook, no human approves payment). Separately, the one money-creating route that DOES exist — POST /api/payments/checkout, rate-limited on its own at server.js:333 — appears nowhere in the spec.
impact: An SDK generated from this file exposes `approvePaymentSlip(id)` and `uploadPaymentSlip()` methods for a payment-approval flow the platform deliberately removed, plus three more dead calls. Five 404s handed to integrators as documented API; the one live checkout door is invisible. Every one of the five returns Express HTML (~1.1KB), not JSON, so a generated client's error path throws on parse rather than reporting 404.
fix: READ-ONLY on money paths per house rules — no route changes proposed here. All five disappear the moment API-01's regeneration runs, because the source JSDoc for them is already gone. Then, separately, add a `@swagger` block for POST /api/payments/checkout (documentation only, no handler change) so the live money door is described.
lane: LANE 4 — the spec, and what it costs to integrate
verdict_reason: Set-difference between the published file and the regenerated spec returns exactly the five claimed (path,method) pairs and nothing else: /api/farms/{id}/qrcode GET, /api/payments GET, /api/payments/slip/upload POST, /api/payments/slip/{id}/approve POST, /api/pricing/invoice/{phase} GET. Nothing exists only in the regenerated spec. Router verification confirms each: payments.js declares only router.post at :208 /create, :356 /phase1/:applicationId, :463 /phase2/:applicationId, :501 /checkout — zero GET handlers, zero /slip/*. pricing.js declares only router.get :229 '/', :251 '/fees', router.post :291 '/calculate'. farms.js carries the Thai deletion note for the farm-level QR door at :265-269 dated 2026-09-05. POST /api/payments/checkout is absent from the published spec (it is not among the 48 ops) and does carry its own paymentLimiter. Finding is read-only on money paths, as required.

title: The only wired code-generation pipeline builds clients from eight fictional microservice specs and auto-commits them to main
evidence: The workflow triggers on push to main/develop for `openapi/**/*.yaml` and runs `openapi-generator-cli generate` over openapi/{access,application,payment,certificate,audit,authentication,pricing}-service.yaml — NOT over docs/api/openapi.json. Those YAMLs describe a system that does not exist: `servers:` in them name api.gacp.platform, staging-api.gacp.platform and api.gacp-botanical.com (authentication-service.yaml:35-38, access-service.yaml:14-17); their paths are `/api/v2/access/check`, `/api/v2/pricing/fees`, `/api/v2/pricing/invoice/{phase}`, `/webhooks/omise`, `/invoices/{invoiceId}/promptpay`. The server mounts only `/api` and `/api/v1` (apps/backend/server.js:375-378, whose comment reads "no /v2 prefix"); grep for `/api/v2` in server.js + routes returns nothing; grep for `omise` in routes/ and services/ returns nothing (payment is Stripe-only). openapi/auth-health.yaml:295-306 defines LoginRequest as `required: [email, password]` — a third contradictory login contract, and one the code explicitly refuses (auth-schemas.js:66-73 rejects email: "เข้าสู่ระบบด้วยเลขบัตรประชาชนเท่านั้น ไม่รองรับอีเมล"). The job runs with `--skip-validate-spec` and `|| echo "⚠️ Warning"`, so nothing can fail it. Output paths `apps/web-app/src/generated/api/` and `apps/mobile_app/lib/generated/api/` do not exist (`ls` on both: absent; the real dir is apps/mobile-app with a hyphen), and `grep -rn "generated/api" apps/web-app/src` returns nothing — no consumer. Lines 117-126 then `git add`/`git commit`/`git push` the output to main with `[skip ci]`. openapitools.json pins generator 7.17.0 but carries no `generators` block and was added in the repo's first commit; @openapitools/openapi-generator-cli is in no package.json.
impact: A CI job that, on any touch to openapi/, writes machine-generated code straight to main unreviewed — colliding with L5 (Tier C + deploy = operator, no auto-push). If it ever produced usable output, that output would be a client for four hostnames that do not resolve and an /api/v2 surface that is not mounted: 100% non-functional. Today it produces nothing anyone imports, so the repo pays CI minutes and governance risk for zero value.
fix: Smallest correct version: delete .github/workflows/generate-api-clients.yml and openapitools.json (2 files). If client generation is genuinely wanted later, re-add it pointed at docs/api/openapi.json, without `--skip-validate-spec`, and emitting an artifact for review rather than `git push` to main. Separately delete the openapi/ directory (8 YAMLs + README, one commit) or move it under docs/archive/ with a header saying it describes a proposed architecture that was never built — leaving it in place keeps three login contracts alive in one repo.
lane: LANE 4 — the spec, and what it costs to integrate
verdict_reason: Workflow confirmed at .github/workflows/generate-api-clients.yml — triggers on push/PR to main+develop for openapi/**/*.yaml (lines 11-22), generates with --skip-validate-spec plus `|| echo "⚠️ Warning"` so nothing can fail it, and lines 112-126 do `git add`/`git commit`/`git push` on push events with [skip ci]. The specs are fictional: authentication-service.yaml servers at :35/:37/:39 are api.gacp.platform, staging-api.gacp.platform, localhost:3001/v1/auth; access-service.yaml :16 and pricing-service.yaml :16 are api.gacp-botanical.com. /api/v2 paths exist in access-service.yaml (:24,:53,:82) and pricing-service.yaml (:24,:49,:76); grep for 'api/v2' across apps/backend/server.js + routes/ returns nothing, and server.js:384 mounts '/api' with the literal comment '(no /v2 prefix)'. payment-service.yaml:295 defines /webhooks/omise; a word-boundary grep for 'omise' across routes/ and services/ returns nothing (the finding's original grep would have matched 'Promise' — I re-ran it with -w and it is genuinely clean). openapi/auth-health.yaml:295-306 defines LoginRequest as required:[email,password], which auth-schemas.js:69-76 explicitly rejects. Output dirs are absent: apps/web-app/src/generated does not exist, apps/mobile_app does not exist (only apps/mobile-app), grep 'generated/api' in apps/web-app/src returns nothing, and @openapitools/openapi-generator-cli is in no package.json. openapitools.json pins 7.17.0 with no generators block and was added in the first commit e94759c1.
correction: 'Eight fictional microservice specs' is one too many for the generation loop. The SERVICES array lists 8 names but one of them, `auth-Applicant`, has no matching openapi/auth-Applicant.yaml, so the `if [ -f ]` guard skips it and only 7 specs are ever generated. openapi/ does hold 8 YAMLs + README, but the 8th is auth-health.yaml, which the workflow never consumes — so the contradictory email-login contract in auth-health.yaml:295-306 is a stale in-repo document, not something this pipeline emits. The deletion recommendation is unaffected.

title: The entire external-integration surface — 17 public operations including a trust registry, revocation list and signature verifier — is 0% specified, and the spec points integrators at endpoints it does not contain
evidence: I walked the อย./factory path using only docs/api/openapi.json. Searching the file: paths containing 'trace' = [], 'verify' = [], 'public' = [] — zero of each, out of 41 paths. The spec's own GET /api/certificates description says "For public QR verification use the /api/trace/* endpoints — those need no auth", and no /api/trace path is in the document. The only lot-shaped operation it does carry, GET /api/harvest-batches/lot/{batchNumber}, has NO `responses` block at all (harvest-batches.js:190-202 annotates only parameters), so the integrator cannot learn a single field name; and it is not the door the platform actually uses — the buyer-facing scan calls /api/trace/lot/:lotId (trace-batch-lot-routes.js:198). Meanwhile the code has a purpose-built government-integration API at /api/interoperability/v1/* (mounted routes/api/index.js:350) with 14 operations: certificate verify (:157, :168, :179), e-certificate export (:104), signed envelope (:197), POST signatures/verify (:228), trust/public-key (:266), trust/registry (:285), trust/revocations (:343), resolve (:452), trace/events (:477), and two data/event contract documents (:90, :97). Seven need no key at all; six take `x-api-key` (middleware/partner-api-key.js:56, keys from INTEROP_PARTNER_API_KEYS). None of the 14 is in the spec. The spec instead declares an ApiKeyAuth scheme described as "lab webhooks, set via LAB_API_KEY" — and LAB_API_KEY is read by no route in the backend (only two comment mentions), while /api/callbacks has a rate limiter (server.js:334) and a sanitizer bypass (server.js:131) but no router mounted.
impact: Where the อย. developer gets stuck: step 1. The spec offers only BearerAuth and one login that demands a checksum-valid 13-digit Thai national ID they will never hold — so verification appears to require impersonating a farmer. It does not: /api/public/verify/:certificateNumber is open, rate-limited, and returns a machine-readable `reasonCode`, and /api/interoperability/v1/trust/public-key + /v1/signatures/verify allow full offline verification. The best-designed, most externally-important part of this platform is invisible to every integrator who reads the published contract. 17 undocumented public operations = the whole external surface.
fix: Annotate 17 operations, not 648. Tier 1 (10 files touched, all documentation-only `@swagger` JSDoc): the 7 keyless interoperability ops + 3 public certificate-verify ops (public.js:94,278,347) + certificates.js:486 + the 6 trace ops. Tier 2 (6 ops): the partner-key interoperability exports, documented against the ApiKeyAuth scheme that already exists — and fix that scheme's description to name INTEROP_PARTNER_API_KEYS instead of the nonexistent LAB_API_KEY (config/swagger.js:69). Also correct the misleading pointer in the certificates description (certificates.js `@swagger` block) once /api/trace/* is actually in the document. That is 23 operations total, 3.5% of the surface and 100% of the external contract.
lane: LANE 4 — the spec, and what it costs to integrate
verdict_reason: Confirmed on every count. Searching the published spec: zero paths containing 'trace', 'verify', 'public', or 'interoperability' out of 41. The GET /api/certificates description does contain the quoted pointer to '/api/trace/* endpoints — those need no auth' while no such path is in the document. GET /api/harvest-batches/lot/{batchNumber} has parameters and tags but no `responses` key at all. interoperability.js has exactly 14 route declarations and zero @swagger blocks: keyless at :90, :97, :157, :168, :179, :228, :266 (7); requirePartnerApiKey at :104, :197, :285, :343, :452, :477 (6); plus :396 revoke behind authenticatePROVIDER+requireAdminRole. Mounted at routes/api/index.js:350. Partner keys come from middleware/partner-api-key.js:55-62 via x-api-key. public.js:94/:278/:347 and trace.js:62/:86/:125 and trace-batch-lot-routes.js:49/:198 and trace-verification-routes.js:35 all confirmed at the cited lines. certificates.js:486 confirmed. LAB_API_KEY: `grep process.env.LAB_API_KEY` across the backend returns nothing — it appears only in partner-api-key.js:21 (a comment), config/swagger.js:51 and :69. No '/callbacks' router is mounted in routes/api/index.js, yet server.js:343 gives it a webhookLimiter and server.js:131 a sanitizer bypass.
correction: The title's '17 public operations including a trust registry, revocation list and signature verifier' mixes two access tiers. trust/registry (:285) and trust/revocations (:343) are behind requirePartnerApiKey, so they belong to the 6 partner ops, not the 17 keyless/public ones. Only the signature verifier (POST /v1/signatures/verify :228) and trust/public-key (:266) are genuinely keyless. The body of the finding gets this right (7 keyless + 6 keyed); the title does not. Also server.js line refs drift +9 in this finding's neighbourhood (callbacks limiter is :343, not :334) because commit fe289fea landed 19 lines into server.js earlier today.

title: 45 of 48 documented operations have no response schema and no operation documents an error body — the spec cannot generate a usable client even where it is accurate
evidence: Counted over the published file: 48 operations; 18 have no `responses` block whatsoever; only 3 (GET /api/applications/draft, GET /api/audits, GET /api/auth/health/me) have any response carrying `content`. Zero operations declare a `default` response or any error body — every 400/401/404/409/500 entry is a bare description string. The whole document contains exactly one `$ref` (to #/components/schemas/User); the other six component schemas are referenced by nothing. The generator itself knows: generate-openapi-spec.js:88-101 collects missing-responses as WARNINGS and writes the file anyway, with the comment "Routes without declared responses are uninterpretable to integrators". Meanwhile the measured reality is five different success envelopes over 22 endpoints, and an unknown /api path returns ~1.1KB of Express HTML rather than JSON — the measurements confirm this on /api/plots, /api/lots, /api/surveys, /api/training-records, /api/master-data/provinces (all 404, ~1.09KB HTML, and all five have a router mounted at that prefix in routes/api/index.js, so the integrator cannot even distinguish "no such API" from "no collection door on an API that exists"). Reading the code I found a sixth envelope not in the measured set: public.js:107-120 returns {success, verified, valid, data:{status, reasonCode, reason}}.
impact: typescript-axios generated from this file types 45 of 48 responses as `any`/`void` and has no error model at all; the integrator writes the response shape by hand from trial and error, which is precisely how the five-envelope drift keeps growing. Error handling breaks on first contact because the 404 body is HTML, not the JSON every generated client assumes.
fix: Two small, high-leverage additions to config/swagger.js (one file): (1) define `components.schemas.ApiError` matching what shared/api-response.js:118-131 actually emits — {success:false, code, error, message, messageTh, requestId, timestamp, path, method} — and add a top-level `components.responses.Error` that operations can `$ref`; (2) define `components.schemas.Envelope` for {success, data}. Then require `content` only on the 23 external operations from API-04 rather than retrofitting all 48. Separately (one file, apps/backend/server.js) add a JSON 404 handler for the `/api` prefix so an unmatched API path returns the same error envelope instead of HTML — that single change makes every generated client's error path work.
lane: LANE 4 — the spec, and what it costs to integrate
verdict_reason: Recounted over the published file: 48 operations, 18 with no `responses` key at all, and exactly 3 carrying any `content` — GET /api/applications/draft, GET /api/audits, GET /api/auth/health/me. So 45 of 48 have no response schema. Zero operations declare a `default` response. The document contains exactly one $ref (#/components/schemas/User); the other six component schemas (PlantSpecies, HarvestBatch, PreSubmissionValidation, DocumentSlot, PlantUnit, PlantUnitLifecycle) are referenced by nothing. generate-openapi-spec.js:87-101 does collect missing-responses as warnings and writes anyway, carrying the quoted comment. All five measured 404 paths do have routers mounted (index.js:83 master-data, :317 plots, :327 lots, :343 training-records, :355 surveys). The sixth envelope is real: public.js:109-121 returns {success, verified, valid, data:{status, reasonCode, reason}}. The proposed ApiError shape matches shared/api-response.js — respondError/sendErrorResponse emits {success:false, code, error, message, messageTh, details?, requestId, timestamp, path, method} (responseMeta at :80-87, the json() at :124-134).
correction: The second half of the fix is already implemented in this tree and should not be re-proposed as new work. commit fe289fea ('an API that answers HTML has broken its contract'), dated 2026-09-08 02:40 and an ancestor of HEAD, added apps/backend/middleware/api-not-found.js plus server.js:455-457 mounting apiNotFoundHandler on both /api and /api/v1, with an integration test at __tests__/integration/api-answers-json-not-html.test.js. The measured HTML 404 is therefore a stale-deployment fact, not a missing-code fact: the remaining action is to deploy, not to write a handler. The api-response.js line range is :108-134, not :118-131.

title: Two documented operations are mounted only behind a flag that is set in no environment except CI
evidence: routes/api/index.js:384 gates `router.use('/wizard', require('./applications/wizard'))` behind `process.env.ENABLE_PROVIDER_LEGACY_ALIAS === 'true'`. The comment 11 lines above it (index.js:373) states the flag "is set in NO environment (nothing in .env.example / compose / docs references it)". I grepped the whole repo: the only place that sets it is .github/workflows/ci.yml:781 (`ENABLE_PROVIDER_LEGACY_ALIAS: "true"` for the erp-regression job) and two test files. It is absent from every .env and compose file. The published spec documents both operations with no mention of the flag; both are still annotated in the source (routes/api/applications/wizard.js), so a plain regeneration will keep publishing them.
impact: Two of 48 documented operations (4%) 404 in every deployed environment while passing in CI — the worst possible combination, since CI proves them green. An integrator implementing the wizard auto-save loop against the spec gets 404 on staging and production.
fix: Decide, then make the spec say it. If the wizard alias is dead: delete the `@swagger` blocks in routes/api/applications/wizard.js along with the mount at index.js:384-387. If it is live: mount it unconditionally, exactly as the /admin router was un-gated for the same reason (index.js:373-379 records that precedent). Either way, one file plus the regeneration. Do not leave a flag-gated route documented as unconditional.
lane: LANE 4 — the spec, and what it costs to integrate
verdict_reason: routes/api/index.js:384 gates `router.use('/wizard', require('./applications/wizard'))` (:386) behind ENABLE_PROVIDER_LEGACY_ALIAS === 'true', and the comment at :373 does say the flag 'is set in NO environment'. Repo-wide grep confirms the only setter outside tests is .github/workflows/ci.yml:781 for the erp-regression job; provider-cms.js:6 reads it and two test files set it. No .env or compose file sets it. The published spec documents /api/wizard/draft GET+POST with no flag caveat, wizard.js still carries @swagger blocks at :28 and :54, and /api/wizard/draft does NOT appear in my only-in-published set — so a plain regeneration republishes both operations. The /admin un-gating precedent at index.js:370-379 is real and reads exactly as described.
correction: Two nits. The mount block is index.js:384-387 with the wizard line at :386 (the finding's range is right, its prose implies :384 is the wizard line). And 'nothing in .env.example / compose / docs references it' is the code's own comment, not quite true today: scripts/readme.md:11 and :192 document the flag (default false). Neither changes the conclusion — it is set in no deployed environment.

title: The one list operation that does carry an item schema types its id as integer; the column is a uuid string
evidence: The spec declares `id: {type: integer}` and `auditNumber: {type: string}` for each item. The handler at audits.js:110-120 builds each item from an Application row: `id: app.id`, `auditNumber: app.applicationNumber`. application.prisma:4 is `id String @id @default(uuid())`. So the wire value is a uuid string, not an integer. The same annotation also omits four fields the handler actually returns (applicationId, applicantName, inspector, auditMode). This is one of only three operations in the entire document with a typed response, which makes the error load-bearing.
impact: A generated TypeScript client types `audit.id: number`; every id it receives is a uuid string, so any arithmetic, sort, or numeric route-param interpolation silently misbehaves rather than failing loudly. Same class of defect as the PlantSpecies/HarvestBatch component schemas, which also declare `id: {type: integer}` (config/swagger.js:88, 103) — worth checking those models before publishing them.
fix: In routes/api/audit/audits.js, change the item schema to `id: {type: string, format: uuid}` and add the four returned fields. While there, verify config/swagger.js:88 and :103 against harvest.prisma/herb.prisma before those two component schemas get referenced by anything.
lane: LANE 4 — the spec, and what it costs to integrate
verdict_reason: Confirmed at the source. The @swagger block above GET /api/audits (routes/api/audit/audits.js:59-95) declares item properties id:{type:integer}, auditNumber, status, plantType, scheduledDate. The handler at :110-121 builds id: app.id and auditNumber: app.applicationNumber from Application rows, and prisma/schema/application.prisma:4 is `id String @id @default(uuid())` — so the wire value is a uuid string. The annotation omits four fields the handler returns: applicationId, applicantName, inspector, auditMode. This is indeed one of only 3 operations in the whole document with a typed response. The parenthetical about the component schemas also holds: PlantSpecies.id and HarvestBatch.id are both declared integer, while trace.prisma:176 and harvest.prisma:9 are both `id String @id @default(uuid())`; HarvestBatch also declares farmId and speciesId as integer.
correction: The config/swagger.js line numbers are wrong. PlantSpecies.id:{type:'integer'} is at config/swagger.js:82 and HarvestBatch.id:{type:'integer'} at :94 (with farmId :97 and speciesId :98 also wrongly typed integer) — not :88 and :103. The finding's other citations are exact.

title: GET /api/auth/health/me is documented as a six-field User but returns the whole user row minus a ten-name deny-list
evidence: The spec's User schema declares six properties (id, email, firstName, lastName, role, status). The handler chain is auth-health.js:176 → getMe (health-auth-profile-handlers.js:319-320) → `AuthService.getProfile(id)`, which is prisma-auth-service.js:547: `prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { id: userId } })` — no `select`, so every column comes back. The only filter is sanitizeUserPayload (auth-controller.js:63-88), a DENY-list that spreads the row and deletes ten named fields. The User model in prisma/schema/auth.prisma has 73 scalar columns; all ten deny-list names are real columns, leaving up to 63 fields on the wire. Columns that are NOT on the deny-list and therefore ship include healthId, providerId, canonicalId, canonicalIdLegacy, healthIdHmac, providerIdHmac and taxIdHmac — all verified present in the model. I read the code path only; I did not call the endpoint with a token, so I cannot state the exact field count observed on the wire.
impact: The published contract understates the response by roughly an order of magnitude (6 documented vs up to 63 returned), so nobody reviewing the spec can see what this endpoint discloses. It is also bytes on every profile load — a deny-list also means any column added to User in future migrations is published automatically, with no code change and no review.
fix: Replace the deny-list with an allow-list at the source: give prisma-auth-service.js:547 an explicit `select` naming the fields the profile screen and the spec both need, then make the spec's User schema match it exactly. One function, one schema block. An allow-list is the only version of this that cannot regress when a column is added.
lane: LANE 4 — the spec, and what it costs to integrate
verdict_reason: Walked the whole chain. auth-health.js:176 mounts GET /me → AuthController.getMe; the @swagger block above it $refs #/components/schemas/User, which config/swagger.js:137-147 declares with exactly six properties. getMe is controllers/auth-controller/health-auth-profile-handlers.js:308, and lines :319-320 are exactly `const user = await AuthService.getProfile(req.user.id);` / `return sendSuccessResponse(res, req, { data: sanitizeUserPayload(user) });` — the cited line numbers are precise. prisma-auth-service.js:546-548 is `async getProfile(userId) { return await prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { id: userId } }); }` with no `select`. sanitizeUserPayload is auth-controller.js:63-89, a deny-list that spreads the row and deletes exactly ten named fields. I parsed prisma/schema/auth.prisma: model User has 73 scalar columns, and healthId, providerId, canonicalId, canonicalIdLegacy, healthIdHmac, providerIdHmac and taxIdHmac are all present and all absent from the deny-list. 73 − 10 = up to 63 fields on the wire against 6 documented. The finding is explicit that it read the code path only and did not call the endpoint — that honesty is warranted and the claim is scoped to what it proved. The allow-list fix is the right root fix and touches one function plus one schema block.

title: The contract test that should have caught the stale spec asserts a floor of 6 operations against a live 43 and never reads the published file
evidence: The test requires `../../config/swagger` — the in-memory spec — and asserts `pathCount >= 6` and `pairCount >= 6`, with a comment calling 6 the "pre-W4 baseline". The live spec has 36 paths / 43 pairs, so the assertion has ~7x of slack and can never go red. Nothing in the file opens docs/api/openapi.json. That is exactly why 170 leaf-key differences (API-01) accumulated while this test stayed green in every evidence pack in the repo (grep for "passes validateSpec()" hits 25 archived suite runs, all green). The known-drift allowlist in the same file (:87, `KNOWN_UNDECLARED_TAG_ALLOWLIST = ['Audits']`) is a second instance of the same pattern: a real drift converted into a permanent exemption.
impact: A guardrail that is green while the artifact it exists to protect is wrong — the repo's own recurring defect class (memory: "gate asks what the screen never writes"). It cost 114 days of undetected drift and a login contract that cannot work.
fix: Add one assertion to this existing file: `expect(JSON.stringify(require('../../config/swagger'), null, 2) + '\n').toBe(fs.readFileSync(path.join(__dirname,'../../../../docs/api/openapi.json'),'utf8'))` (match the generator's exact serialization at generate-openapi-spec.js:155 — JSON.stringify(spec, null, 2), no trailing newline). Ten lines, one file, and staleness becomes impossible to merge. Raise the >= 6 floors to the current 36/43 in the same edit so the ratchet only moves up.
lane: LANE 4 — the spec, and what it costs to integrate
verdict_reason: Verified the test file. __tests__/unit/openapi-spec-generation.test.js:29 requires ../../config/swagger (the in-memory spec) and the assertions at :49-61 are `expect(pathCount).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(6)` and `expect(pairCount).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(6)`, with the header comment at :12-15 calling 6 the pre-W4 baseline. Live values are 36 paths / 43 pairs, so the floor has ~6-7x of slack. `grep openapi.json` in that file returns nothing — it never opens the published artifact, which is exactly how 170 leaf-key differences accumulated behind a green test. KNOWN_UNDECLARED_TAG_ALLOWLIST = new Set(['Audits']) is at :87 as claimed, and is indeed a real drift converted into a permanent exemption.
correction: The proposed assertion snippet is self-contradictory and would fail as written: it appends `+ '\n'` while the same sentence says 'no trailing newline'. I checked the artifact — docs/api/openapi.json ends in `}` with no trailing newline, and the generator writes `JSON.stringify(swaggerSpec, null, 2)` at scripts/generate-openapi-spec.js:159-160 (not :155). The correct assertion is `expect(JSON.stringify(require('../../config/swagger'), null, 2)).toBe(fs.readFileSync(specPath,'utf8'))` with no appended newline.

title: The spec's table of contents advertises nine empty sections, two unused auth schemes, and two schemas the code deleted for exactly this reason
where: docs/api/openapi.json components.schemas.PlantUnit / PlantUnitLifecycle and tags[]; apps/backend/config/swagger.js:145-151

title: A documented list endpoint answers 200 success:true with an empty array when its query throws
evidence: The handler's catch block is `logger.error(...); res.json({ success: true, data: [] })` — HTTP 200, success true, empty list, on any failure of listPendingScheduleAudits. The published spec documents only a 200 "List of pending applications" for this operation, so the contract offers no way to tell the two apart. The sibling handler four lines above (audits.js:127-130) at least uses `res.status(500).json({success:false, data:{audits:[]}})`, so the two neighbouring endpoints disagree about what a failure looks like.
impact: An integrator polling this endpoint cannot distinguish "nothing pending" from "the database round trip failed" — and at 244ms per query to Sydney, transient failures are the realistic case, not the hypothetical one. A scheduler built on it silently stops working and reports healthy.
fix: Change the catch to `return respondError(res, req, error, { message: 'Failed to list pending-schedule audits' })`, the helper this file's neighbours already use, and document 500 in the operation's `@swagger` block. Two lines. This is a green-mask instance and the repo already has check-green-mask-assertions.js as an ACTIVE probe — worth checking whether its scope can be extended to catch `catch { res.json({success: true` in route handlers generally.
lane: LANE 4 — the spec, and what it costs to integrate
verdict_reason: Exact. routes/api/audit/audits.js:145 declares GET /pending-schedule, and its catch at :149-152 is `logger.error(...)` followed by `res.json({ success: true, data: [] })` — HTTP 200, success true, empty list, on any throw from listPendingScheduleAudits. title: Every authenticated request pays two strictly-sequential Sydney round trips before the handler starts
evidence: authenticateHealth does `const identity = await fetchIdentityFromDb(resolvedUserId, decoded)` (line 502 → `authDbClient.user.findUnique` at :160) and only then `return bindScopes(req, res, next)` (line 536). bindScopes = tenantContextMiddleware → activeEntityMiddleware, and activeEntityMiddleware always issues its own query: `prisma.entityMembership.findUnique` (active-entity-middleware.js:121) on the header fast path — and the web client sends `x-active-entity-id` on every call (apps/web-app/src/lib/api/api-client.ts:304-312), so that path is the live one. Both queries key off `resolvedUserId`, taken from the decoded JWT; neither reads the other's output, so the sequencing is incidental, not required. Live router walk of the booted app: 452 of 611 unique routes sit behind authenticateHealth/Provider/Any. Arithmetic check against the measurements: GET /api/invoices/my = identity + entityMembership + invoiceService.listByApplicant (routes/api/finance/invoices.js:81) = 3 queries × 244 ms = 732 ms, against 813 ms measured internally for a 26-byte empty array.
impact: ~244 ms of pure, avoidable serialization on 452 of 611 routes (74% of the reachable surface). /api/invoices/my 813 ms → ~570 ms internal; /api/applications/my 1180 ms → ~940 ms. The 993 ms public-edge median of 16 GETs drops by roughly a quarter. Nothing about the payload changes — this is latency spent waiting on a query whose result the other query never needed.
fix: Run the two independent lookups concurrently. Split activeEntityMiddleware into resolve-then-enter (resolveActiveEntity is already a standalone function at active-entity-middleware.js:110), then in each authenticate* function replace the sequential pair with: `const [identity, activeEntity] = await Promise.all([fetchIdentityFromDb(resolvedUserId, decoded), resolveActiveEntity({ user: { id: resolvedUserId }, headers: req.headers })]);` and have bindScopes enter the AsyncLocalStorage scope from the already-resolved value instead of querying. Keep the existing `if (!identity.dbHealthy) return next()` branch — it just discards the pre-resolved entity. Touches 2 files. The deeper fix (one LEFT JOIN via $queryRaw, 488 ms → 244 ms) is a follow-up: Prisma `include` would not help, since it issues a separate query per relation.
verdict_reason: Locations verified: auth-middleware.js:502 `await fetchIdentityFromDb` then :536 `return bindScopes`, bindScopes at :42 = bindTenant → bindActiveEntity; active-entity-middleware.js:120-121 issues `prisma.entityMembership.findUnique` on the header fast path; api-client.ts:304-312 sends x-active-entity-id on every browser call. The same sequential pair repeats at :653/:688, :833/:866, :900/:925. On the header path the two reads genuinely key off resolvedUserId only and never read each other, so the serialization is incidental — real ~244ms.
correction: Three corrections. (1) The proposed `resolveActiveEntity({ user: { id: resolvedUserId }, headers: req.headers })` BREAKS the no-header path: the fallback findPersonalEntity (active-entity-middleware.js:88-107) reads `reqUser.healthId`, which only exists after fetchIdentityFromDb. Passing a stub user makes it return null → activeEntity middleware calls next() with no entity scope → the personal `personal:true` applicant pin silently disappears for any client that does not send x-active-entity-id (curl, mobile, integrators). Parallelise ONLY when req.headers['x-active-entity-id'] is present; keep the sequential path otherwise. (2) Error precedence changes: with Promise.all, a 403 ACTIVE_ENTITY_MISMATCH can now pre-empt the 401 session-epoch rejection at :508-516 — resolve the identity rejection first before acting on the entity result. (3) The '452 of 611' route count is not independently verified here; 312 of 648 route declarations name authenticate* inline, the rest inherit via router.use, so a router-walk figure is plausible but unchecked.

title: The two most likely failure responses on this API — unknown path and rate limit — are not JSON
where: apps/backend/server.js:229-237 (globalLimiter) and the absence of any 404 terminator after server.js:378
evidence: Ran the exact globalLimiter option set from server.js:229-236 with max lowered to 1: request 2 returned `status=429 content-type=text/html; charset=utf-8` with the body `Too many requests from this IP, please try again later.` — express-rate-limit's default handler is `response.send(message)` (node_modules/express-rate-limit/dist/index.cjs:829), and a string argument makes Express send text/html. This limiter is mounted `app.use('/api', globalLimiter)` (server.js:239) and is the ONLY limiter over ~640 of the 648 handlers. Separately, server.js mounts routers at :377-380 and then jumps straight to the 4-arg error handler at :442 — there is no 3-arg catch-all, so an unmatched /api path falls through to Express's default HTML 404. The probe confirms it live: /master-data/provinces, /plots, /lots, /training-records and /surveys all returned `(non-json)` at 1085-1102 bytes. The web client guards its parse (`try { errorData = await response.json(); } catch { errorData = null; }`, api-client.ts:358), so the user gets a generic message and the `Retry-After: 900` that IS on the wire never reaches them.
impact: Two failure modes on a 648-route API return an unparseable body: the global 429 (the only rate limit most routes have) and every 404 on a mistyped or retired path. ~1.1 KB of HTML per 404 instead of ~120 bytes of JSON. Any integrator doing `res.json()` gets a parse exception rather than an error object; the platform's own client silently degrades to a generic banner on rate-limit.
fix: Two additions to server.js. (1) Give globalLimiter a handler instead of a `message` string, matching authRateLimitHandler at :219: `handler: (req, res) => res.status(429).json({ success: false, code: 'RATE_LIMITED', error: 'Too many requests from this IP, please try again later.', requestId: req.id })` — Retry-After is already set before the handler runs (dist/index.cjs:993-995), so it survives. (2) Immediately before the error handler at :442, add `app.use('/api', (req, res) => sendErrorResponse(res, req, { status: 404, code: 'NOT_FOUND', message: `Cannot ${req.method} ${req.path}` }));` — sendErrorResponse and the NOT_FOUND catalogue row already exist (shared/api-response.js:100, shared/error-codes.js NOT_FOUND).
verdict_reason: The 429 half is confirmed by re-running globalLimiter's exact option set (max lowered to 1): request 2 came back `429 content-type: text/html; charset=utf-8` with the plain string body, and `retry-after: 900` on the wire. globalLimiter still carries `message: 'Too many requests...'` instead of a handler, and it is the only limiter over most of /api.
correction: Both halves need restating. (a) Line refs are stale: globalLimiter is server.js:239-246, mounted `app.use('/api', globalLimiter)` at :293 — not 229-237/:239. (b) The 404 half is ALREADY FIXED on HEAD: commit fe289fea (2026-09-08 02:40, i.e. after the measurement) added middleware/api-not-found.js and mounts it at server.js:456-457 for /api and /api/v1, before the error handler at :460, answering JSON 404 and 405+Allow. The live HTML 404s the probe saw are a stale deployed image, not the tree. What remains actionable is only the one-line globalLimiter handler change.

title: The global input sanitizer silently rewrites ordinary Thai free text before it is stored
evidence: Ran sanitizeValue() from the module on realistic field values. `'ผู้ติดต่อ contactPerson=สมชาย ใจดี'` → `'ผู้ติดต่อ cสมชาย ใจดี'` (the /on\w+\s*=/gi pattern at :17 matched inside the word "contact"). `'ราคา -- 500 บาท ต่อกิโลกรัม'` → `'ราคา 500 บาท ต่อกิโลกรัม'` (/--\s/g at :28). `'แปลง A1 /* โซนเหนือ */ ปลูกกัญชา'` → `'แปลง A1  ปลูกกัญชา'` (/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g at :27 ate everything between the delimiters). `'monitoring_enabled=true'` → `'mtrue'`. sanitizeValue mutates and returns; sanitizeInput assigns the result back over req.body (:95-97). The mount at server.js:131-135 covers every path except /api/callbacks, so this runs before every handler on all 205 POST and 31 PUT routes. Detections are logged at :112 but the request proceeds with the mutated value.
impact: Applicant-authored free text — addresses, chemical-history details, mitigation plans, correction-round replies, auditor notes — is silently altered between the browser and the database on a government certification platform. The stored, reviewed and certified string is not the string the farmer typed, and nothing in the response says so. The /*…*/ case is unbounded: any text between those two delimiters disappears entirely. The SQL patterns buy nothing against injection here (every query goes through Prisma's parameterized client); they only cost integrity.
fix: Change the action from silent rewrite to loud refusal — strictly stronger than today and consistent with this repo's fail-loud style. In sanitizeInput, collect `detections` without reassigning req.body/req.query, and when `detections.length > 0` return `sendErrorResponse(res, req, { status: 400, code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR', message: 'Input contains characters that are not allowed', details: detections })`. Retiring the three prose-matching patterns (:17, :27, :28) is the correct second step but is a guardrail change — CLAUDE.md §8 requires operator sign-off, so raise it rather than doing it.
verdict_reason: Re-ran sanitizeValue() from middleware/sanitize-input.js: 'ผู้ติดต่อ contactPerson=สมชาย ใจดี' → 'ผู้ติดต่อ cสมชาย ใจดี'; 'ราคา -- 500 บาท ต่อกิโลกรัม' → 'ราคา 500 บาท ต่อกิโลกรัม'; 'แปลง A1 /* โซนเหนือ */ ปลูกกัญชา' → 'แปลง A1  ปลูกกัญชา'; 'monitoring_enabled=true' → 'mtrue'. Patterns at :17, :27, :28 as named; sanitizeValue returns and sanitizeInput reassigns over req.body/req.query at :95-101; detections only logged at :111-118 and the request proceeds mutated. Mount covers everything except /api*/callbacks.
correction: Mount is server.js:130-136 (not 131-135). More important: the proposed 400-on-detection is not strictly stronger for the farmer — 'ราคา -- 500 บาท' is legitimate Thai prose and would become a hard submission refusal instead of a silent edit. Ship the 400 together with retiring the three prose-matching patterns (:17 /on\w+\s*=/, :27 /\/\*…\*\//, :28 /--\s/), not with the retirement deferred, or the fix trades corruption for a blocked applicant. Prisma parameterisation means those three buy nothing anyway.

title: The sanitizer's req.params branch never runs — the documented path-parameter protection does not exist
where: apps/backend/middleware/sanitize-input.js:105-108 (and its doc comment at :86-91), mounted at apps/backend/server.js:131-135
evidence: The comment at :86-91 states path parameters are sanitized in place so "downstream route handlers see clean values". Ran a minimal Express app that mounts the real sanitizeInput at app level, exactly as server.js:131-135 does, in front of `GET /farms/:farmId`: the app-level middleware printed `req.params = {}` and the route handler then received `req.params = {"farmId":"abc--%20DROP"}` — untouched. Express populates req.params per-layer during routing, which happens after every app.use() middleware has already run, so the branch at :108 always operates on an empty object.
impact: A protection that is documented, mounted, logged about and dead. It is the exact 'guards match shape, not declaration' class already recorded in this repo's memory — the mount proves the middleware runs, not that it can see the thing it claims to guard. Any future reviewer reading server.js will believe path params are cleaned when no path param has ever been cleaned.
fix: Delete lines 105-108 and the paragraph of the doc comment at :86-91 that promises it, so the file stops asserting a protection it does not provide. If path-param cleaning is actually wanted, it has to be mounted per-router (router.use inside each route file, after the path is matched) — but note that Prisma parameterizes every query, so this branch was buying little even in intent. Ship the honest deletion first; treat re-adding it as a separate decision.
verdict_reason: Reproduced with a real Express app mounting the actual sanitizeInput at app level in front of GET /farms/:farmId: the app-level layer printed `req.params = {}` and the handler received `{"farmId":"abc-- DROP<script >"}` untouched. Express fills req.params per routing layer, after every app.use has run, so the branch always operates on an empty object. The doc comment does promise the protection.
correction: Line refs: the params branch is :107-108 (its comment :103-106) and the doc paragraph is :85-91, not :105-108/:86-91. Delete both, and note module.exports at :123 also exports sanitizeValue, which unit tests use — leave that intact.

title: Refund is the one money path whose idempotency check sits outside its own transaction, with no DB constraint behind it
evidence: initiateRefund reads the guard at line 321 — `const existing = _readRefundBlock(invoice)` against Invoice.metadata JSON — and only opens `prisma.$transaction` thirty lines later at :351, inside which it creates, issues and posts a credit note and then merges the refund block into Invoice.metadata. Two concurrent calls both read no refund block and both proceed. The cap check inside credit-note-service (assertWithinInvoiceCap, credit-note-service.js:219-268) sums prior credit notes, but under READ COMMITTED both transactions see prior = 0 and both pass. There is no unique index to stop the second write: prisma/migrations/20260516030000_add_credit_debit_notes/migration.sql:61 creates `credit_notes_originalInvoiceId_idx` as a PLAIN index, and prisma/schema/billing.prisma:862-876 declares no @@unique on originalInvoiceId. Its two siblings do it properly and prove the house pattern: checkout is guarded by the partial unique `uniq_invoice_app_service_active` (migration 20260701010000:87-89) with a P2002 → 409 translation at stripe-checkout-service.js:695-700, and quotations by `quotations_application_issuer_live_uq` (migration 20260828100000:86-88) with _isUniqueViolation at quotation-service.js:531-534.
impact: A double-clicked Refund button in the staff console can post two credit notes, each reversing the full invoice, against one paid invoice — the ledger double-reverses and the trial balance is wrong by the invoice total. Reachable by ACCOUNT_PLATFORM/ADMIN only, and the only limiter in front is the global 1000/15min, so the two requests need only land within one round trip of each other (244 ms, which is exactly what a double-click produces). READ AND PROPOSE ONLY — per CLAUDE.md L3 no agent may run this migration.
fix: Proposed for operator review, not applied. Expand-only DDL, matching the two sibling constraints: `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX CONCURRENTLY "credit_notes_original_invoice_live_uq" ON "credit_notes" ("originalInvoiceId") WHERE "isDeleted" = false AND "status" <> 'CANCELLED';` — run the duplicate-check query first, in the same shape as migration 20260828100000's preamble. Then in refund-service.js catch the unique violation with the existing `_isUniqueViolation` helper shape and return the same idempotent payload the :321 branch already builds. Both halves need operator merge (Tier C).

title: A complete 385-row error catalogue exists and 89.5% of error responses never put the code on the wire
where: apps/backend/shared/error-codes.js (385 rows) vs 1177 error-response sites across apps/backend/routes/ and apps/backend/controllers/
evidence: Brace-matched every `res.status(4xx|5xx).json({…})` argument in routes/ and controllers/: 1177 sites, of which 124 (10.5%) carry a `code:` key. The catalogue itself is healthy — comparing its 385 keys against every UPPER_SNAKE `code:` literal in routes/services/shared/middleware found 0 catalogued codes with no source literal. The canonical emitter that does attach the code, sendErrorResponse (shared/api-response.js:100-127), has only 57 call sites in routes/controllers. The key name for the human string is also unsettled: 807 sites use `error` only, 186 use `message` only, 179 use both, 5 use neither. Localized keys are spelled `messageTh` (46 sites), `errorTh` (14, routes/api/identity/mfa.js + routes/api/audit/audits.js) and `messageEN` (8, consumer-feedback.js + trace/lots.js + helpers/lots-utility-routes.js). The measured 400 body {success,message} is reproducible at routes/api/cultivation/planting-cycles.js:106 — and that same handler answers 401 at :110 and 404 at :115 under `error`, so the string moves keys between statuses within one function. The platform's own client branches on exactly one code in the whole catalogue (apps/web-app/src/lib/api/api-client.ts:97, ACTIVE_ENTITY_MISMATCH_CODE).
impact: An integrator building against this API today can branch on HTTP status and nothing else; to distinguish 'farmId missing' from 'farm not found' they must string-match Thai or English prose that no test pins. The 385-row catalogue, its Thai messages and its remediation hints are effectively write-only.
fix: Do not sweep 1053 sites at once — that is a >10-file change with no behavioural test behind it. Smallest correct version: add `function fail(res, req, status, code, message)` to shared/api-response.js delegating to sendErrorResponse, then convert only the money, identity and certificate write doors (routes/api/finance/**, routes/api/auth/**, routes/api/certificates/**, routes/api/admin/certificates.js) — about 180 sites in 14 files, each code already present in the catalogue.
